L75: ABSTRACT
L76: 
L77: In this paper, a novel semisupervised algorithm is proposed
L78: with spatial similarity for classi ﬁ cation of hyperspectral data
L79: 
L80: based on the transductive support vector machines algorithm.
L81: 
L82: The proposed method exploits the characteristic of the hyper-
L83: 
L84: spectral data, in which spatially nearby points are likely to
L85: 
L86: belong to the same class. To utilize this assumption, a novel
L87: 
L88: transductive support vector machines algorithm is proposed.
L89: 
L90: Experimental tests are performed on two hyperspectral data
L91: 
L92: sets. The results show that the proposed algorithm obtains
L93: higher classi ﬁ cation accuracies.
L94: 
L95: Index Terms—Image classi ﬁ cation, kernel methods,
L96: 
L97: transductive support vector machines, spatial similarity
L98: 
L99: 1. INTRODUCTION
L100: 
L101: Earth observation images by satellite sensors provide diverse
L102: 
L103: information for environmental monitoring services. In order
L104: 
L105: to make the images usable for monitoring purposes, super-
L106: 
L107: vised classi ﬁ cation methods are mainly utilized due to their
L108: 
L109: ability to make more accurate classi ﬁ cation results. Note that
L110: the success of supervised classi ﬁ cation methods depends on
L111: 
L112: the quantity and quality of labeled samples. Nevertheless, the
L113: 
L114: process of collecting training samples is time-consuming and
L115: 
L116: expensive in most cases. To avoid a selection of too many
L117: 
L118: training samples, one way is to utilize the information con-
L119: 
L120: tained in the massive unlabeled samples. The method is called
L121: 
L122: semisupervised learning (SSL) method [1].
L123: 
L124: SSL is a very active ﬁ eld of machine learning and has at-
L125: tracted wide research interests in remote sensing image classi-
L126: 
L127: ﬁ cation. Among the most successful SSL methods, the Trans-
L128: 
L129: ductive Support Vector Machines (TSVM) [2] try to max-
L130: 
L131: imize the margin for both labeled and semilabled samples,
L132: 
L133: which are obtained based on the current classi ﬁ cation hyper-
L134: 
L135: planes. In [3], the information c ontained in labeled samples is
L136: 
L137: propagated to their neighbors via graphs until the whole im-
L138: 
L139: age obtains a global steady state. In [4], the SVM decision

L149: 
L150: remote sensing image classi ﬁ cation tasks [5]. In [6], Tuia et
L151: 
L152: al. proposed a Bagged kernel using the k-means algorithm to
L153: 
L154: deform the standard kernel.
L155: Despite their good performances and simplicity, these
L156: 
L157: methods seldom consider spatial characteristics of remote
L158: 
L159: sensing images. Remote sensing images are spatially contin-
L160: 
L161: uous due to the fact that the land cover types in the Earth are
L162: 
L163: continuous. Hence, if one pixel belongs to one land cover
L164: 
L165: type, e.g., cropland, it is plausible that the spatially nearby
L166: 
L167: pixels also belong to cropland without other information.
L168: 
L169: Since SSL methods try their best to exploit the unlabeled
L170: samples to improve the classi ﬁ cation model, they should also
L171: 
L172: utilize this intuitive assumption.
L173: 
L174: In this paper, a novel transductive SVM is proposed based
L175: 
L176: on the above idea. The structure of this paper is organized
L177: 
L178: as follows: Section 2 presents the proposed algorithm, after
L179: 
L180: brie ﬂ y describing the TSVM algorithm; Section 3 presents
L181: 
L182: two hyperspectral data sets used and experimental results and
L183: 
L184: discussions; and Section 4 ﬁ nally draws the conclusion of this
L185: 
L186: work.
